### sphere3d

This example utilizes a D3Q7 stencil to validate the macroscopic radiative transfer lattice Boltzmann method (RTLBM) to approximate the Helmholtz equation.
The derivation of the Helmholtz equation that approximates the radiative transport equation (RTE) is

$$
\Delta \Phi = \mu_{\text{eff}}^{2} \Phi
$$ {#eq-Helmholtz}

with

$$
\mu_{\text{eff}} =  \sqrt{3 \mu_a ( \mu_a + \mu_s )},
$$ {#eq-effAttCoefficient}

where

- $\mu_\mathrm{a}$ is the absorption coefficient and
- $\mu_\mathrm{s}$ is the scattering coefficient.

Here, $\Phi$ refers to the radiative energy flux.
The Helmholtz equation is solved similarly to the advection-diffusion equation.
The LBM is validated against an analytical solution that is known for the target Helmholtz equation, @eq-Helmholtz, in a particular setup.
The radius of the sphere is $R$ and the radiative source is placed at radius $r_\mathrm{0} = 0.1 R$ and equipped with a Dirichlet boundary.
Similarly, the outgoing Dirichlet boundary is placed at radius $r_\mathrm{1} = R$.

![Cross section of the spherical benchmark with cell size $\triangle x$. Yellow indicates the radiative source, blue the participating volume and gray the outgoing boundary.](/examples/radiativeTransport/sphere3d/doc/fig/sphericalDomain_radiation.png){#fig-domain-radiation width="60%"}
